full_judgment:
The appellants herein as the plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 19 of 1972 in the Additional Court of Sub-ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Noakhali for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in respect of 9.73 acres of land by removing structures therefrom and for recovery of mesne profit. 

 5. The trial Court decreed the suit on contest in part and the plaintiffs' title in respect of 3.09 acres of land was declared and khas possession was also allowed by evicting defendant No. 1 therefrom. On appeal by the plaintiffs in Title Appeal No. 115 of 1989, the appellate Court allowed the appeal and decreed the suit in full in respect of 9.73 acres of land and the cross-objection of the defendant was rejected. 

 21. A court of law cannot pass a decree in respect of land which is not specified How the trial Court could pass such a part decree in respect of an unidentified land is shrouded in mystery. In a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession the plaintiffs are not only required to prove their title to the suit land and but also to prove that the suit has been filed within twelve years from the date of alleged dispossession. From the evidence of the PWs, it appears that the plaintiffs could not prove that the suit has been filed within twelve years from the date of dispossession. Admittedly, defendant No. 1 was in possession of the suit land prior to the purchase of the plaintiffs. The part decree passed by the trial Court in favour of the plaintiffs appears to be a gratuitous decree and there is no scope for passing such decree.
